rounds.text: Hexa Tradex exhibits a profound disconnect between its market valuation and its underlying operational performance, evidenced by a staggering P/E ratio of 570x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 186.46x, which dwarfs the sector benchmark of 12.98x [E11]. The company’s inability to generate meaningful returns is highlighted by a median return on equity of 0% over the last decade [E24] and a current ROE of -0.2% [E13]. Furthermore, the business is currently destroying value through its operations, as evidenced by negative free cash flow of Rs -3.63 Cr [E34] and a cash conversion ratio of only 0.42x [E32]. A discounted cash flow analysis suggests an intrinsic value of just Rs 11 per share, implying a massive margin of safety deficit of -1288.7% [E43, E44]. While the stock is technically lagging, with a relative-strength rating of 28 [E49] and a price currently below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E48], the market continues to price in an unrealistic 57.2% earnings growth rate [E45]. Conceded: the company maintains a conservative financial structure with no debt [E35] and trades at a price-to-book ratio of 0.15x [E2].
